newsitem.title: UK: British female student guilty of stalking lecturer.
newsitem.headline: British female student guilty of stalking lecturer.

text.p: A mature female student was found guilty on Wednesday of stalking her male lecturer and ordered by a British court to pay him damages for stress.

Eileen McLardy, 50, was ordered not to "molest, harass or stalk" Dr Robert Fine, not to go within 200 yards (metres) of his home and to pay 5,000 pounds ($8,250) damages to the senior lecturer for the "stress and strain" she had caused him.
For two years Fine had been the object of a vendetta by McLardy, a mother of three, and her husband that was described by the judge as malicious, obsessive and bizarre.

The case was believed to be the first time a Briton had won damages for being stalked. The harassment known as stalking is normally carried out by a man on a woman. The government plans to make it a criminal offence in the next few months.
McLardy had accused Fine, her lecturer at Warwick University in central England, of sexually harassing her.
"She has conducted a vendetta against Dr Fine and the reason for it seems to me because of a frivolous complaint against him of sexual harassment," the judge told London's High Court.
"When that was rejected she seems to have embarked upon this course of conduct."
